news.title: FIFA to visit potential 2030 World Cup host cities in November and December
news.lede: FIFA will carry out a series of visits to candidate host cities in Spain, Portugal and Morocco in November and December as part of the venue selection process for the 2030 World Cup, world football's governing body said on Tuesday. A FIFA delegation will visit candidate cities and stadiums in all three host countries to assess their suitability to host games. FIFA has yet to confirm which venues will be included, and has not announced where the World Cup final will be held, with Spain and Morocco battling to hold football's biggest match. Visits are planned for Agadir, Casablanca, Fez, Marrakech, Rabat and Tangier in Morocco; Lisbon and Porto in Portugal; and Barcelona, Bilbao, Las Palmas, Madrid, San Sebastian, Seville and Zaragoza in Spain.

news.title: Morocco U15 Finish 13th at World Cup in Azerbaijan With 36 Goals
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U15 national football team finished 13th in the 2026 U15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, ending their campaign with an impressive attacking record of 36 goals. The tournament brought together 189 countries, with Morocco securing eight victories in ten matches despite suffering elimination in the round of 16 against Paraguay. The Atlas Cubs began their campaign with five consecutive victories in the group stage, demonstrating their attacking strength from the opening match. Morocco defeated the Philippines 2-0 before securing a 4-2 victory over Costa Rica.

news.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
news.lede: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambition was to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”

news.title: FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup: Kenya makes history as Africa showcases its future stars
news.lede: Kenya’s Junior Starlets reached a historic milestone at the 2026 FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco,after they qualified for the Round of 16, helped in particular by a resounding 4–0 win over Samoa. Kenya’s success is part of a broader trend; alongside Morocco, Nigeria, and Ghana, four of the five African teams in the competition have reached the round of 16, a first in the tournament’s history.
